title: Why the DRG side is the frontier
objective: Explain why spinal/DRG visceral afferents are a current research frontier.

steps.title: The understudied line
steps.body: The **vagal** side of interoception has been studied for decades. The **spinal/[[DRG]]** side — especially how genetically-defined subtypes innervate specific organs — is only now being mapped, thanks to mouse genetics and single-cell tools. That gap is the lab's whole opening.

steps.prompt: Why is the spinal/DRG side of visceral sensing described as a 'frontier'?
options: Its organ-specific subtypes are only now being defined and manipulated
No one had recorded from spinal visceral afferents until recently
Its subtypes were fully defined long ago; only their roles are unknown
Spinal afferents turned out to outnumber vagal ones in every organ
steps.explanation: New genetic and single-cell tools finally let researchers define DRG visceral subtypes and test their functions — work that wasn't possible before, unlike the long-studied vagal side.

variants.setup: Vagal interoception is well studied; the DRG side less so.
variants.prompt: Why is the DRG side a frontier now?
options: Its subtypes are only now definable and testable
It was never recorded from until recently
Its subtypes were all defined long ago
variants.reveal: Modern genetic tools newly allow defining and manipulating DRG visceral subtypes.

steps.setup: Your lab wants to extend the DRG-afferent map from the colon to the pancreas.
steps.prompt: What makes this a novel contribution?
options: The pancreas isn't yet mapped the way the colon is, so it's new territory
Pancreatic DRG afferents have never been seen, so any found are new
The pancreas is innervated only by the vagus, so DRG fibers are new
The colon map is already known to apply to the pancreas unchanged
steps.reveal: The DRG-afferent story has been built mostly in the colon; applying that playbook to the pancreas extends the map to an organ it doesn't yet cover — exactly why your project is novel.

variants.prompt: Mapping pancreas DRG afferents is novel because…
options: The pancreas isn't yet mapped like the colon
No DRG fibers have ever been seen there
Only the vagus innervates the pancreas
variants.explanation: It extends the colon playbook to an unmapped organ.

sources.note: Spinal (DRG) vs vagal innervation of the gut; the DRG side is the frontier.

reviewNotes: DRG visceral afferents as frontier; ties to the pancreas project.
